content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3: targeted overtime at the peak hours, cancel coaching and offer callbacks on payments. It is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target (81.7%) for 08:30-15:15, at ₹12,900.","why":"Payments has had 11 agents against 17 planned since 08:00. Most of the gap is lateness from the bus strike (8 agents), plus 1 sick. Call volume is near normal (+8.4%), so the problem is missing staff, not extra calls. General is also short (8 absences against a usual 2.4), so it can't lend agents to payments. Doing nothing leaves the window at 63.0%. The cheaper plans can't fix a staffing gap: P1 reaches only 63.2% and P2 only 71.5%. P3 adds overtime on both queues in the busiest hours. It lifts the window to 81.7% (payments 86.6%, general 75.3%), cuts abandons to 3.5% from 8.2%, and raises rest of day to 87.3%.","trade_offs":["Cost: ₹12,900, against ₹2,652 for P2. P2 still misses target at 71.5%, with 5.5% of callers abandoning.","Other queue: general reaches only 75.3% under P3, below the 80% target, though up from 59.5% with no action. P4 brings general to 83.6% but costs ₹4,152 more (₹17,052).","Risk: the result depends on enough agents accepting overtime (up to 10 on payments and 8 on general per block). If uptake is short, the plan will fall back towards target or below it.","Coaching is cancelled for the whole window."],"watch":"Track overtime acceptances by 10:00, and service level on general from 11:00. If payments uptake falls short, or general stays well below 75%, consider adding P4's chat deflection and general callbacks. Also check whether the late agents start arriving early as the strike eases, which would reduce the overtime needed."}
